identificationModule.briefTitle: Short Course Radiotherapy Followed by CAPOX and Carrilizumab and Bevacizumab or Cetuximab for the Initial Treatment of Unresectable Metastatic Rectal Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase II, Single-center Study of Short-course Radiotherapy Followed by CAPOX and Carrelizumab and Bevacizumab or Cetuximab in the Treatment of Initially Unresectable Metastatic Rectal Cancer

leadSponsor.name: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

descriptionModule.briefSummary: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of short-course radiotherapy followed by CAPOX and carrilizumab and bevacizumab or cetuximab in the initial treatment of unresectable metastatic rectal cancer

interventions.name: CAPOX+ Camrelizumab+ Cetuximab
interventions.description: For advanced primary treatment of unresectable rectal cancer, primary radiation therapy DT 25Gy/5F, and rest for 1 week, followed by CAPOX chemotherapy + Camrelizumab + Bevacizumab or Cetuximab (KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF all wild-type Cetuximab, KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF variants selected Bevacizumab) for 4-6 months, after which Capecitabine + Camrelizumab + Bevacizumab or Cetuximab was maintained

interventions.name: CAPOX+ Camrelizumab+ Bevacizumab
interventions.description: For advanced primary treatment of unresectable rectal cancer, primary radiation therapy DT 25Gy/5F, and rest for 1 week, followed by CAPOX chemotherapy + Camrelizumab + Bevacizumab or Cetuximab (KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF all wild-type Cetuximab, KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF variants selected Bevacizumab) for 4-6 months, after which Capecitabine + Camrelizumab + Bevacizumab or Cetuximab was maintained

primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From enrollment to initial efficacy evaluation,assessed up to 6 months

secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From enrollment to the first appearance of disease progression or date of deathfrom any cause,whichever came first, assessed up to 18 months
From enrollment to patient death,assessed up to 36 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Adverse Event (AE), Treatment-Emergent AE (TEAE), Adverse Event of SpecialInterest (AESl) and Serious Adverse Event (SAE)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events will be assessed by investigator(s) according to CommonTerminology Criteria for Adverse Events Version 5.0 (CTCAE v5.0).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Through out the study (up to 36 months)
